newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Lever Bros Pakistan profit seen up.
newsitem.headline: Lever Bros Pakistan profit seen up.

text.p: Lever Brothers Pakistan Ltd is likely to report higher profits for 1996/97 (July-June) following completion of its merger with its main competitor, Brooke Bond Pakistan Ltd, analysts say.

The two multinational firms, which have already merged worldwide, announced last week that approval by their shareholders and the Sindh province High Court had cleared the last obstacles to sealing their new partnership in Pakistan. The new firm will operate as Lever Brothers Pakistan Ltd, with Britain's Unilever Plc as its ultimate holding company.
"The merger will eliminate competition in the tea business, cut overhead costs and improve profitability," said Yasin Lakhani, former head of the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE).

Lever and Brooke Bond had both complained that their business was under pressure from large-scale smuggling of Kenyan tea into Pakistan via Iran and Afghanistan without payment of duty and tax equivalent to 107 percent of C&F value.
Lever's 50-rupee share closed unchanged at 720 ($17.78) on Friday. A broker said financial institutions had bought 3,000 Lever shares at 760 rupees and 4,000 at 780 on Thursday.
Lever sells consumer items such as cooking oil, soap, detergents, ice-cream and Lipton brand tea, while Brooke Bond used to blend and market tea, and sell other kitchen items.

Lever paid a 100 percent dividend on its 50-rupee share and Brooke Bond a 302.5 percent dividend on its 10-rupee share for the 18 months ended June 30, 1996. The two firms changed their financial year to July-June from January-December last year.

Lever paid a 30 percent interim dividend and Brooke Bond 35 percent for the first half ended on December 31, 1996. Lever's paid-up capital, previously 499.425 million rupees, has risen to 619 million with the addition of Brooke Bond's paid-up capital of 119.529 million rupees. A KSE official said that merger arrangements had set the value of one 50-rupee ordinary Lever share at 4.3 of Brooke Bond's 10-rupee ordinary shares. Brooke Bond's books will be closed from June 11 to 17 to complete the deal.
"The merger will have a positive impact on stock prices," said Nadir Shah, chief dealer at Jardine Fleming in Karachi, adding that Lever's scrip was very stable.

Lever opened a 700-million-rupee Wall's ice-cream plant near Lahore in 1995, when Pakistan became the newest market in Asia for the brand, introduced in Indonesia in 1992 and China and India in 1993. The large and fast-growing market for ice-cream in Pakistan was estimated at 26 million litres in 1994.
"Lever is planning new investments of more than one billion rupees in a number of projects, mainly in the food sector," said a Lever director, who asked not to be named. He gave no details.
